evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4.148: tabellae tribūtāriae, letters of credit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Traupman’s word, and a well-founded one: Cicero’s tabellae tribūtāriae are letters of credit. Traupman prints the adjective with a long first i; Lewis & Short has tribūtārius, from tribūtum.
Our earlier description, before Traupman’s word was noticed.

sources: Lewis & Short: tabella · Lewis & Short: tributarius
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 213, 298.
David Morgan and Patrick Owens, Adumbratio Lexici Anglico-Latini, s.v. credit card.

phrases.latin: Praesentāriam pecūniam nōn habeō. Ecce autem meam tabellam tribūtāriam.
phrases.english: I don’t have the cash. But here’s my credit card.
